solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Root is quite excellent?

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent or cool
the suffix -ish means somewhat or quite

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly praises a root as being pretty good.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read back to front from the clue: excellent-ish is the same as quite excellent, and the question mark admits the playful construction.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a plant grown for its edible, peppery root vegetable.

clue.text: Current advert promoting Queen's comeback

indicators.note: promoting moves something up to the top, and Queen is the regal abbreviation, so that letter moves to the front

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a poster is an advertisement on a wall

explanation.surface: A topical advert gives prominence to the Queen's return.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of the advert is R for Regina, the Queen; promoting it shifts that last letter to the very front.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort, a verbal comeback in an exchange.

clue.text: A new helper upset Roman goddess

indicators.note: in a down clue, to upset is to turn upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
an aid is a helper or assistant

explanation.surface: A newly hired helper offended a Roman goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon.

clue.text: Joined relatives in Messina, and we sit around

indicators.note: around suggests letters thrown about in all directions into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Family members visiting the Sicilian port of Messina sit about with us.
explanation.definitionFit: Siamese twins are conjoined twins, siblings physically joined at birth.

clue.text: Need rocks in garden

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it about, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A garden needs rocks, as in a rockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived, and by extension any paradise-like garden.

clue.text: Committed leaders of democratic enterprise took part in election

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letters are taken

parts.note: first letters of the two words
to take part in an election is to vote

explanation.surface: Dedicated heads of a democratic business cast their ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted means dedicated or committed to a cause or person.

clue.text: A street in American city is unpleasant

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, framed by the city

parts.note: NY is New York
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A street in some American city is a grim place.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and unpleasant are synonyms, describing something disagreeable.

clue.text: Smoker from the south wanted to get naked

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading from bottom to top
stripping naked removes the outer clothing, so the outside letters are taken off

parts.note: the word with its outer letters stripped; that the answer also runs forwards across 'get naked' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A smoker from the south wanted to strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' suggests a person with a cigarette; it is a volcano, which smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active Sicilian volcano, which regularly emits smoke.

clue.text: I will say sex with one friend is improper

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
e.g. means for example, i.e. say
it is a coy word for sex
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone declares that sleeping with a friend is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegitimate means not allowed by law or rules, so not proper.

clue.text: Nice sheds left for agricultural labourer

indicators.note: to shed something is to cast it off, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: nice means pleasant
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: It reads as the French city of Nice shedding something for a farm worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised at the start, 'Nice' looks like the French city, but it is just the adjective meaning pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a poor smallholder or farm worker, traditionally working the land.

clue.text: Is very entertained by falsehoods

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within their home, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: falsehoods are lies
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone is greatly amused by untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a verb starting the sentence, but it is the definition: to be is to live.
explanation.definitionFit: To live is to exist, so 'lives' substitutes for 'is' in the sense of existing.

clue.text: Draw adapted metal seat

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch a modified metal chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb about sketching; it is the noun for a tied game.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalemate is a chess position in which neither side can win, a kind of tied result.

clue.text: Conservative ignoring Republican plaything

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician brushes off an American Republican as a mere plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy is an object for a child to play with.

clue.text: Apprentice scratching head is one getting paid

indicators.note: scratching means striking out, and head means the first letter, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: an apprentice is a learner

explanation.surface: A puzzled trainee scratches their head over being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' suggests a puzzled gesture, but it means removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is someone who receives wages or income for work.

clue.text: Carefree Orwell regularly sacked

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
to be axed is to be sacked from a job

explanation.surface: The writer George Orwell is repeatedly fired without a care.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed means calm and untroubled, the same as carefree.

clue.text: Women's group's party beginning to make sense

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation; the possessive adds S
a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is the only part kept

parts.note: first letter of make

explanation.surface: A women's group's party starts to make sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a long-established British community organisation for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom and sense are synonyms, both meaning sound judgement.

clue.text: Bodywork expert to regret turning up after service

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means flipping to read from the bottom

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A car bodywork specialist regrets showing up after a vehicle service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bodywork' suggests car panels; here it is work on a human body.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur is someone who massages the body professionally.

clue.text: Age limit restricts set

indicators.note: to restrict is to hold within bounds, so the answer is held inside the words

parts.note: found spanning the two words

explanation.surface: An age limit restricts a set group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to set or solidify, as a jelly does.

clue.text: Entrances very rich man

definitions.meaning: first meaning: openings in a fence or wall
second meaning: Bill ..., the Microsoft co-founder and billionaire

explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrances' could also be the verb meaning enchants, which leads nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Gates are hinged barriers forming entrances, and Bill Gates is among the world's richest people.

clue.text: Mostly wine and dine with snobs on vacation, in flatulent state

definitions.note: a noun phrase matching the noun answer

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the next word, so wine loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short
taken as written

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: taken as written before its inside is emptied

explanation.surface: Someone treating guests to food and drink with snooty company, ending up full of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wine and dine' reads as one phrase, but 'and' only links: WIN (wine without its last letter), DINE, then SS from snobs with the middle vacated.
explanation.definitionFit: Windiness is the condition of having gas in the gut, which is what flatulence means.

clue.text: A flat, for one, not close to habitable

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: last letter of habitable

explanation.surface: A flat that is nowhere near habitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A flat' looks like an apartment; it is the musical pitch, and 'for one' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is one musical note, a semitone below A on the scale.

clue.text: Old Father Time, who lives abroad

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun

parts.note: ex- means former or old
pa is an informal word for father
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Old Father Time, the personification of time, living overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Father Time' reads as a single figure, but it splits into three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat, short for expatriate, is a person residing outside their native country.

clue.text: Poison cricket team to stop century

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred, as in a cricket century
a cricket team is an eleven, written XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A plot to poison a cricket team so they cannot score a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a century is 100 runs by one batter; a ton is the everyday word for that hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poisonous substance, especially one produced by a living organism.

clue.text: Tramp disturbed a priest

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of its proper order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vagrant disturbed a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun for a vagrant; it is the verb meaning to walk wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk heavily or wearily, the same as to tramp.

clue.text: Perhaps left small fish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Perhaps only small fish were left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the past tense of leave; it is the noun naming a side, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Left is one example of a side, the other being right.

clue.text: Cured gambler

definitions.meaning: first meaning: recovered from an illness
second meaning: one who places a bet

explanation.surface: A gambler who has been cured of the habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a coinage: one who bets is a 'better', usually spelt bettor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone recovered from illness is said to be better, and a person who bets is a better.
